name: Daryl Trent
home: the blocks north of the port
life: “I still remember my first pension notice arriving on a postcard.” People around Tideline Market know Daryl by a small Saturday habit. Daryl picks out the bruised fruit first and asks the seller what will ripen by supper.
voice: My pension owns a sliver of this firm. I want the tenants to know we're tied together.
appearance: Daryl has a blunt cut just below the ears, heavy brows and an unusually delicate jaw, and a favorite piece of clothing, a charcoal zip cardigan. It usually goes with a comb in a sleeve sewn into the lining. When somebody else has the floor, Daryl squares up pieces of paper while thinking.
personality: Daryl prefers exact instructions at work and pleasant surprises at home. The two standards occasionally collide, especially when a relative thinks dropping by counts as notice.
agenda: To introduce the tenant association to the pension trustee.
family: Mateo Alston is Daryl’s cousin. Daryl chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. Mateo brings a spare shopping bag. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *A sail cut small*, Mateo says, “I know where my old racing rival patched the sail.”
connections: Iva Allard. The missing signature makes the trustee ask whose stake the ledger didn't show.

reactions.situation: A family member wants the ledger locked away
reactions.response: Daryl asks whether the heirs can look at copies without parting with the old ledger.

reactions.situation: A diner goes silent in the middle of a noisy family celebration
reactions.response: Daryl takes a small plate to the quieter end of the table and saves the seat beside it.
